root_cause.text: The fwctl class initialization was deferred until module_init time, which runs after CXL's module_init due to link order in drivers/Makefile, causing device_add() to skip knode_class initialization when fwctl_class is not yet registered, leading to an uninitialized knode that triggers a NULL pointer dereference during device_del().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `module_init(fwctl_init)` to `subsys_initcall(fwctl_init)`, which runs earlier in the boot sequence before module_init calls. The CVE description explicitly states that "CXL is linked before fwctl in drivers/Makefile. Both use `module_init`, so `cxl_pci_driver_init()` runs first" and that when `device_add()` is called, "fwctl_class is not yet registered because fwctl_init() hasn't run, causing `class_to_subsys()` to return NULL and skip knode_class initialization." This initialization ordering mismatch between CXL probe (which calls fwctl_register and device_add) and fwctl class registration is the root cause.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change fwctl initialization from module_init to subsys_initcall to ensure the framework is available earlier for dependent subsystems.
intent_record.what: Changed the module initialization macro from `module_init(fwctl_init)` to `subsys_initcall(fwctl_init)` on line 418.
intent_record.how: This changes the initialization order of the fwctl module. `subsys_initcall()` causes the initialization function to be called earlier in the kernel boot sequence (at subsystem initialization level) compared to `module_init()` (which runs at module initialization level). This ensures fwctl_init executes before other modules that may depend on the fwctl framework being available.

commit 2e4986cf2d525eed3a240b7821f89ca45cf36d78
Author: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@ziepe.ca>
Date:   Thu Feb 27 20:26:29 2025 -0400

    fwctl: Add basic structure for a class subsystem with a cdev
    
    Create the class, character device and functions for a fwctl driver to
    un/register to the subsystem.
    
    A typical fwctl driver has a sysfs presence like:
    
    $ ls -l /dev/fwctl/fwctl0
    crw------- 1 root root 250, 0 Apr 25 19:16 /dev/fwctl/fwctl0
    
    $ ls /sys/class/fwctl/fwct
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability exists in this commit because the fwctl_class is registered in module_init() (line 147-158), which runs after CXL's module_init due to link order in drivers/Makefile. The _alloc_device() function at line 65 sets 'fwctl->dev.class = &fwctl_class' (lines 71 and 76), and fwctl_register() calls cdev_device_add() (line 123) which internally calls device_add(). When device_add() is called before fwctl_class is registered, the knode_class initialization is skipped because the class is not yet registered. This leaves knode uninitialized, causing a NULL pointer dereference later during device_del() in fwctl_unregister() (line 141). The code does not check if fwctl_class is registered before calling device_add(), nor does it defer device registration until after the class is available. The fix would require either ensuring fwctl_class is registered before any device_add() calls, or deferring device registration until after module_init completes.
